title: Empirical Standards for Software Engineering Research, Version 0.2.0 (ACM SIGSOFT Paper and Peer Review Quality Task Force; ed. Paul Ralph)

edges.target: Weller 2001, Editorial peer review: strengths and weaknesses
edges.ref: Ann Weller, 2001. Editorial peer review: Its strengths and weaknesses. Information Today, Inc.
edges.evidence: Empirical research consistently shows that peer review is unreliable and ineffective.1

edges.target: Ralph 2016, Practical suggestions for improving peer review (CAIS)
edges.ref: P. Ralph (2016) Practical suggestions for improving scholarly peer review quality and reducing cycle times. CAIS, (38), Article 13.
edges.evidence: Empirical research consistently shows that peer review is unreliable and ineffective.1 ... The current system of peer review is demonstrably biased in many ways.5, 6
edges.section: Introduction (fn 1); Justice, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (fn 6)

edges.evidence: The standards are hosted on the Empirical Standards GitHub repo.2 ... transitioned all completed standards to plain text (GitHub markdown) to facilitate version control and pull requests.
A prototype structured-review system4 is under development, but more help will be needed here.

edges.target: Bravo et al. 2018, Hidden connections: network effects on editorial decisions
edges.ref: Bravo, Farjam, Grimaldo Moreno, Birukou, Squazzoni. 2018. Hidden connections: Network effects on editorial decisions in four CS journals. J. Informetrics 12(1):101-112.
edges.evidence: The current system of peer review is demonstrably biased in many ways.5, 6 One purpose of developing these empirical standards is to make peer review less biased.

edges.target: Inter-Rater Reliability and Agreement Supplement (Cohen's Kappa / Krippendorff's Alpha)
edges.ref: See the Inter-Rater Reliability and Agreement Supplement. (fn 7; part of the Empirical Standards)
edges.evidence: we estimate inter-rater agreement using a statistic like Cohen's Kappa or Krippendorff's Alpha.7 When agreement among raters is high, we are more confident in the ratings.
edges.section: The Scientific Basis of Empirical Standards (fn 7)

edges.evidence: We know that peer reviewers exhibit low inter-rater agreement.8
edges.section: The Scientific Basis of Empirical Standards (fn 8)

edges.target: Bullock & Tubbs 1987, case meta-analysis method (raising inter-rater reliability via decision rules)
edges.ref: R. J. Bullock and M.E. Tubbs, 1987. The case meta-analysis method for OD. Research in organizational change and development, 1, pp.171-228.
edges.evidence: scientists figured out how to improve inter-rater reliability decades ago.9 ... You keep defining decision rules to guide raters until sufficient agreement is reached.
edges.section: The Scientific Basis of Empirical Standards (fn 9)

edges.target: Plint et al. 2006, Does the CONSORT checklist improve RCT reports? (systematic review)
edges.ref: Plint, Moher, Morrison, Schulz, Altman, Hill, Gaboury. Does the CONSORT checklist improve the quality of reports of RCTs? A systematic review. MJA 185(5) (2006): 263-267.
edges.evidence: a significant body of research demonstrates that checklists improve consistency and performance in diverse settings including research reporting10 and healthcare11.
edges.section: The Scientific Basis of Empirical Standards (fn 10)

edges.target: Treadwell et al. 2014, Surgical checklists: a systematic review
edges.ref: Treadwell, Lucas, Tsou. Surgical checklists: a systematic review of impacts and implementation. BMJ Quality & Safety 23.4 (2014): 299-318.
edges.evidence: checklists improve consistency and performance in diverse settings including research reporting10 and healthcare11.
edges.section: The Scientific Basis of Empirical Standards (fn 11)

not_reuse_examples: EasyChair and HotCRP: named only as editorial-management systems to integrate with in future; not used or built upon.
'Existing published guidance' on which each standard was drafted (Design Process): mentioned generically with no specific references in this PDF, so no edge can be recorded.

The individual standards (General, Experiment, Case Study, Survey, Multi-Methodology Supplement, Information Visualization Supplement) are the paper's own product, not prior work, except the IRR supplement which is cited as the source of a method.
notes: Position/guidelines report (v0.2.0, 20 pp.) describing the standards and structured review; this PDF is the overview only and does NOT contain the individual standards' 'Suggested readings', so reuse edges are limited to the 11 footnotes (mostly premises about peer-review unreliability/bias and checklist efficacy).
